original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: In only Phase B of the pinned PR1087 selected provider, count one-skipped-child placements of the PR #1866 (3,1,1,1)->6 block whose four selected children have ranks 1,1,1,3 on distinct registers, whose skipped child register is disjoint, and whose intervening scalar events touch none of the selected registers; compute exact GF(2) source/target frame unions and apply the zero-overhead 5-percent ceiling gate.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a general block decoder or effective-rank bound. This run narrows it to one exact inherited tensor, one provider phase, and one skipped-call schedule with a no-buffer register-disjoint commutation rule, to test a concrete source-placement mechanism left open by the consecutive-window study.
bottleneck_link: A rank-six child would replace three rank-one and one rank-three children at equal paid rank mass, the profile lever measured by the selected complex local-word ceiling. Phase B is a pinned source for testing whether that more efficient block can actually be placed.
stop_rule: Enumerate every length-five climb-call window and each interior skipped position 1, 2, or 3 in both Phase B orientations. Require selected ranks {1,1,1,3}, four distinct selected registers, skipped register disjointness, and scalar-gap register disjointness. Stop if fewer than 135 candidate blocks remain, since 135 is the exact zero-overhead 5-percent threshold; do not expand to other gaps or phases in this cycle.
evidence: Both pinned Phase B orientations have 3,870 events (1,952 climbs, 1,918 scalar operations) and histogram {1:1160,2:352,3:344,4:96}. Each has 12 consecutive rank/register windows and 67 raw one-skip windows meeting the rank/register conditions. Every raw one-skip window has scalar crossings on selected registers (63 have two, four have twelve), leaving zero candidates in the claimed commuting class. The package stores exact source/target GF(2) union bases for all 67 raw windows. Even granting all 67 plus all 12 consecutive windows simultaneously and waiving all added costs, the exact moment-only ceiling at 79 blocks is below the 5-percent target; exact controls still place the boundary at 134 failing and 135 passing. No selected construction or kappa change follows.

open_questions.question: Does the same one-skipped-child block have a viable placement in another pinned selected-provider phase under an explicit scalar-crossing tariff?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A different phase may offer more rank/register candidates, while the current result only excludes a narrow Phase B commuting class.
open_questions.first_step: Pin the other phase event interval and adapt this exact rank/register/frame-union census; before enumeration, charge its scalar crossings and compare the candidate ceiling with the 135 zero-overhead threshold.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires a new cycle scope and phase-specific scalar compensation and restoration model; those costs are deliberately waived only for the current upper-bound screen.
